'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Gaza war]]
**At least six [[Palestinians]] are killed when an [[Israel]]i tank fires at a wedding hosted in a school-turned-shelter in [[Gaza City]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/12/19/us-to-host-qatari-turkish-and-egyptian-officials-for-gaza-ceasefire-talks (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa]]
**Eight people are killed, including four attackers, and 15 others are injured in a suicide attack by unidentified militants on a military post in [[North Waziristan District]], [[Khyber Pakhtunkhwa]], [[Pakistan]]. [https://apnews.com/article/pakistan-militants-attack-military-post-northwest-ed59e39adaa78b2a1df30f006a9222f7 (AP)] [https://amu.tv/216694/ (Amu Television)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Mining industry of the Democratic Republic of the Congo]]
**The [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]] suspends artisanal [[Copper mining in the Democratic Republic of the Congo|copper]] and [[cobalt]] processing, ordering operators to halt activities and certify mineral origins while a new commission verifies traceability and legality to curb illegal exports. [https://www.reuters.com/sustainability/boards-policy-regulation/congo-halts-artisanal-copper-cobalt-processing-amid-corruption-crackdown-2025-12-23/ (Reuters)]
*[[Restrictions on TikTok in the United States]]
**Social media platform [[TikTok]] announces a deal to sell 80.1% of its [[United States]]-based assets to a consortium of companies, including [[Oracle Corporation|Oracle]], [[Silver Lake (investment firm)|Silver Lake]], [[MGX Fund Management Limited|MGX]], and existing [[ByteDance]] investors, to avoid a ban in the US. [https://www.dw.com/en/tiktok-us-deal/a-75234707 (DW)]
*[[Uganda]] restricts imports of [[Starlink]] [[Satellite Internet access|satellite internet]] equipment by requiring [[Uganda People's Defence Force|military]] clearance for related devices. [https://www.reuters.com/sustainability/society-equity/uganda-restricts-imports-starlink-equipment-weeks-before-election-2025-12-23/ (Reuters)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russo-Ukrainian war]], [[Ukraine–European Union relations]], [[Foreign involvement in the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Foreign involvement in the Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**[[Confiscation of Russian central bank funds]]
***The [[European Union]] agrees to loan €90 billion (US$105 billion) to [[Ukraine]] from its internal budget after failing to use frozen [[Russia]]n assets. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/2025/12/18/european-union-summit-ukraine-belgium-russia-frozen-assets/ (''The Washington Post'')] [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/ukraine-welcomes-90-billion-euro-eu-loan-despite-lack-deal-russian-assets-2025-12-19/ (Reuters)]
*[[Immigration policy of the second Trump administration]], [[2025 Brown University shooting]]
**The [[U.S. government]] suspends the [[Diversity Immigrant Visa]] scheme for [[green card]]s after the [[Brown University]] shooting suspect was revealed to be from [[Portugal]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c4gp4ze002mo (BBC News)]
*[[The Bahamas–Kosovo relations]]
**[[The Bahamas]] becomes the 110th country to recognize [[Kosovo]] as an independent state. [https://opm.gov.bs/joint-statement-by-the-commonwealth-of-the-bahamas-and-the-republic-of-kosovo-on-recognition-and-the-establishment-of-diplomatic-relations/  (Office of the Prime Minister)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2025 Bondi Beach shooting]]
**[[Australia]]n [[Prime Minister of Australia|prime minister]] [[Anthony Albanese]] announces a nationwide [[gun buyback program]], the largest since the aftermath of the [[Port Arthur massacre (Australia)|1996 Port Arthur massacre]], in response to the recent [[Bondi Beach]] shooting in [[Sydney]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/asia-pacific/20251219-australia-unveils-gun-buyback-and-national-reflection-day-after-bondi-beach-attack (AFP via France 24)]
*[[2025 Taipei stabbings]]
**Three people are killed and five more injured in a [[mass stabbing]] near a [[Metro station|subway station]] in [[Taipei]], [[Taiwan]]. The perpetrator, who also threw [[smoke bomb]]s at the train station, dies during the chase with [[National Police Agency (Taiwan)|police]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/china/several-injured-attack-taipei-media-reports-2025-12-19/ (Reuters)]
*[[Caning in Singapore]]
**[[Singapore]] announces that [[scam]]mers will face mandatory [[caning]] of up to 24 strokes from December 30 under changes to the [[Criminal law of Singapore|criminal law]] passed by [[Parliament of Singapore|parliament]] in November. [https://apnews.com/article/singapore-caning-scam-law-4f12fbbf443ba7ec2227c4800ca1efa0 (AP)]
*[[December 2025 Bangladesh violence]]
**Protests and [[riot]]s erupt across [[Bangladesh]] after the [[assassination]] of activist [[Osman Hadi]] by two members of the banned [[Awami League]] party. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2025/12/19/live-violence-breaks-out-in-bangladesh-after-prominent-protest-leader-dies (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Epstein Files Transparency Act]]
**The [[U.S. Department of Justice]] releases a heavily redacted fraction of the [[Epstein files]], potentially violating the law that determines their full release by December 19. The department intends to continue releasing remaining files over subsequent weeks. [https://apnews.com/live/donald-trump-news-updates-12-19-2025 (AP)] [https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2025/dec/19/epstein-files-release-deadline (''The Guardian'')]
